questions.question: What is the easiest way to know your trailer is skidding?

options.text: Look in your mirrors to see if the trailer left its lane.
Release the brake pedal and push it down again.
Watch for the jackknife warning light on the control panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in your mirrors to see if the trailer left its lane.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to spot a trailer skid. When you brake hard, check your mirrors to make sure your trailer is in the correct position.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Only to test the trailer brakes.
Together with the brake pedal while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve controls the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing. Using it while driving can cause a skid. Do not use it for parking because it may release air pressure and let the brakes go.

questions.question: What is the service air line connected to?
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: How can you tell if your vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: A sticker on the control panel.
A yellow light on the instrument panel.
The letters "ABS" on the brake pedal.
A metal plate inside the driver's side door.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow light on the instrument panel.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle has ABS if it has a yellow ABS warning light on the instrument panel.

questions.question: When should you turn off the retarder for safety?

options.text: When roads are wet, snowy, or icy.
When you are carrying a passenger.
When you are carrying a heavy load.

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are wet, snowy, or icy.
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces braking. However, it can cause wheels to skid on slippery roads. Turn off the retarder when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid driving aggressively?

options.text: Plan trips without extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Do not make hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make hand gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan extra time for traffic delays. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane. Do not make gestures or shake your head at other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver confronts you, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Ignore their gestures. Do not try to challenge them by speeding up.

questions.question: How should trailers be positioned in a double or triple combination?

options.text: Cargo weight must be spread evenly between all trailers.
The heavier trailer should be directly behind the cab.
The heavier trailer should be in the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heavier trailer should be directly behind the cab.
questions.explanation: In a double or triple, the heavier trailer should be positioned right behind the tractor.

questions.question: How can you make your vehicle more visible at dawn or dusk?
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, and in snowy or rainy conditions, turn on your headlights so other drivers can see your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the best way to recognize your trailer is beginning to skid?
questions.explanation: The earliest and best way to spot a trailer skid is to see the trailer move off-course in your mirrors.

questions.question: If a tire rim is damaged, what should you do?

options.text: Weld it to repair the damage.
Move it to the axle farthest from the driver.

questions.explanation: Welded wheels or rims are not safe to use.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes too quickly?

options.text: A whipping motion that can cause the vehicle to roll over.
Other drivers will be confused about which lane you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: A whipping motion that can cause the vehicle to roll over.
questions.explanation: Quick lane changes in a combination vehicle can cause a whipping motion that results in a rollover.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, how far ahead should you look?
questions.explanation: Look 12 to 15 seconds ahead to spot hazards early. At highway speeds, this equals about one quarter mile.

questions.question: If you find something unsafe during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Continue the trip and see a mechanic after.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Avoid using the unsafe items but continue driving.

questions.explanation: You must fix any unsafe problems before driving. It is illegal to operate an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: What color warning light shows when the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working properly?
questions.explanation: The ABS warning light is usually yellow. If the ABS fails, your regular brakes will still work.

questions.question: What is true about driving too fast?

options.text: It is a good way to reach your destination quickly.
It is safe on dry roads.
It is acceptable in light traffic.

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of fatal crashes. Never exceed the speed limit and adjust your speed to match road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do before driving down a hill?
questions.explanation: Shift into a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will make your vehicle speed up as you go down.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer continues in a straight line.

questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, it can swing around and cause a jackknife.

questions.question: When can brakes get out of adjustment?
questions.explanation: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly if they overheat from heavy use. Check brake adjustment often.

questions.question: Which part of a combination vehicle is most likely to roll over?
questions.explanation: The whipping motion makes the last trailer most likely to roll over. Be extra careful when turning with double or triple trailers.
